title: Market uncertainty and existing alliance partners
x: Market uncertainty: prior-year mean monthly stock-price coefficient of variation of sampled industry peers, excluding focal firm
y: Annual count of additional alliances with existing alliance partners
setting: An established firm operates in an industry with multiple potential alliance partners. Its existing alliance ties and own firm-specific volatility are held fixed when comparing lower and higher market uncertainty. Existing partners mean firms with which it has already formed an alliance; no prior success is assumed.
task: Rate how increasing market uncertainty changes the number of additional alliances formed with existing partners in the following year. Compare lower X (Lower industry-peer mean volatility) with higher X (Higher industry-peer mean volatility). Use the same X contrast in both contexts. A positive rating means higher X is associated with more Y; a negative rating means less Y. Rate the relationship, not the overall level of Y. Do not interpret this judgment as a measured empirical coefficient.
sharedFacts: The outcome is the number of additional alliances with existing partners during the following year, not the proportion choosing an existing partner.
The market-uncertainty contrast is held identical across the reference and candidate contexts.

sourceEvidence.citation: Beckman, C. M., Haunschild, P. R., and Phillips, D. J. (2004). Friends or Strangers? Firm-Specific Uncertainty, Market Uncertainty, and Network Partner Selection. Organization Science, 15(3), 259-275. doi:10.1287/orsc.1040.0065.
sourceEvidence.measurementNotes: Firm-specific volatility and existing alliance network held constant
sourceEvidence.translationNotes: Do not equate volatility with an invented forecast error; do not add successful prior projects; count is not a preference share.
